findings.quote:
br_spec = nlmsg_find_attr(nlh, sizeof(struct ifinfomsg), IFLA_AF_SPEC);

	nla_for_each_nested(attr, br_spec, rem) {
findings.reason: Cross-function form of the seed invariant on snapshot s03 (a form the prior s03 artifacts left unexamined; i40e/ice were only audited on s02). Untrusted source: a userspace rtnetlink RTM_SETLINK/PF_BRIDGE message; the dispatcher rtnl_bridge_setlink (net/core/rtnetlink.c:4886-4920) fetches its own br_spec = nlmsg_find_attr(nlh, sizeof(struct ifinfomsg), IFLA_AF_SPEC) and guards it with 'if (br_spec)', but on the BRIDGE_FLAGS_SELF path it forwards the RAW nlh to dev->netdev_ops->ndo_bridge_setlink(dev, nlh, flags, extack) at line 4920, delegating the IFLA_AF_SPEC presence decision to the driver callback. IFLA_AF_SPEC is policy-optional (net/core/rtnetlink.c:1855 '[IFLA_AF_SPEC] = { .type = NLA_NESTED }', no required semantics), and nlmsg_find_attr returns NULL when absent, so an attacker-crafted message with IFLA_BRIDGE_FLAGS=BRIDGE_FLAGS_SELF and no IFLA_AF_SPEC yields br_spec == NULL. Violated invariant (validated != used, cross-function): the caller-side 'if (br_spec)' guard in the dispatcher does NOT cover the driver's independent re-fetch; i40e_ndo_bridge_setlink (drivers/net/ethernet/intel/i40e/i40e_main.c:12752-12777, registered via .ndo_bridge_setlink = i40e_ndo_bridge_setlink at line 13277) performs no presence check of its own on the exact attribute it consumes. Unsafe use: the NULL local br_spec is passed as the nesting attribute into the macro wrapper nla_for_each_nested(attr, br_spec, rem) at line 12776, which expands to nla_for_each_attr(pos, nla_data(nla), nla_len(nla), rem) and immediately dereferences the NULL pointer (nla->nla_len read) — the same NULL-attribute-into-nested-helper mechanism as the seed. Consequence: NULL-pointer-dereference kernel oops (local DoS) from a netlink message crafted to reach this driver path. Counterevidence checked: the s02-twin finding (fact f003/i009) verified the sibling drivers bnxt, be2net, ixgbe and mlx5 all guard with 'if (!br_spec) return -EINVAL;' before the identical loop; on this snapshot the i40e site at 12774-12776 and the identical ice site at 6651-6653 were read directly and both lack any NULL check between the nlmsg_find_attr assignment and the nla_for_each_nested use; rtnl_bridge_getlink/setlink core paths are guarded (4886-4888, 4963-4965).

findings.quote:
br_spec = nlmsg_find_attr(nlh, sizeof(struct ifinfomsg), IFLA_AF_SPEC);

	nla_for_each_nested(attr, br_spec, rem) {
findings.reason: Same cross-function mechanism in the second unguarded driver on s03. Untrusted source: userspace RTM_SETLINK/PF_BRIDGE netlink message forwarded with the raw nlh from rtnl_bridge_setlink's BRIDGE_FLAGS_SELF path (net/core/rtnetlink.c:4920, err = dev->netdev_ops->ndo_bridge_setlink(dev, nlh, flags, extack)). Violated invariant: ice_bridge_setlink (drivers/net/ethernet/intel/ice/ice_main.c:6637-6676, registered via .ndo_bridge_setlink = ice_bridge_setlink at line 6979) fetches br_spec = nlmsg_find_attr(nlh, sizeof(struct ifinfomsg), IFLA_AF_SPEC) at line 6651 with NO NULL/presence check — neither its own nor the dispatcher's covers this independent re-fetch, and the IFLA_AF_SPEC policy entry at net/core/rtnetlink.c:1855 is plain optional { .type = NLA_NESTED }, so an attacker message omitting IFLA_AF_SPEC passes core validation. Unsafe use: the NULL local is passed as the nesting attribute to the nla_for_each_nested macro wrapper at line 6653, whose expansion calls nla_data(nla)/nla_len(nla) on it (NULL deref). Consequence: kernel NULL-pointer-dereference oops (local DoS) from the crafted RTM_SETLINK message. Counterevidence checked: lines 6643-6653 read directly — no 'if (!br_spec)' between assignment and use; the sibling guard pattern exists in other drivers per the s02 audit; core dispatch paths guard their own copies.

candidates.reason: i40e_ndo_bridge_setlink: br_spec from nlmsg_find_attr (12774) fed to nla_for_each_nested (12776) with no NULL check; rtnl_bridge_setlink forwards raw nlh on BRIDGE_FLAGS_SELF (rtnetlink.c:4920); IFLA_AF_SPEC optional in ifla_policy (1855).
ice_bridge_setlink: identical unguarded br_spec into nla_for_each_nested (6651->6653); same dispatcher path and optional policy entry.

rtnl_bridge_setlink guards its own br_spec with 'if (br_spec)' (4887) before nla_for_each_nested (4888); the trailing memcpy(nla_data(attr),...) in the loop path only runs under have_flags set in the same guarded iteration; rtnl_bridge_dellink is identically guarded (4963-4965). The gap is only in the drivers it forwards raw nlh to.

lib/nlattr.c helper functions (validate_nla_bitfield32, nla_policy_len, nla_strscpy, nla_strdup, nla_memcmp etc.) are the core attribute primitives; they dereference their nlattr* parameter by contract (documented non-NULL) and every in-tree caller passes an already-validated attribute from a parse loop or guarded slot; they are the library itself, not handler dispatch surfaces.

nft_parse_register (9191) and nft_parse_u32_check (9178) dereference their attr parameter without NULL checks, but they are library helpers for expression init callbacks; the prior s03 unchecked-tb-deref audit (fact f011) verified the highest-density expression consumers (nft_ct select_ops gating) and the nested-parse audit (fact f002/i012) verified the nf_tables nested-parse sites are slot-guarded; the remaining deep expression-by-expression pass belongs to the kind-callback-tb-gaps branch (i019), not this helper-parameter branch.

The OVS flow_netlink.c/action parsers (29 helper-parameter deref candidates, the largest cluster on s03: genev/erspan_tun_opt_from_nlattr, validate_and_copy_set_tun, ovs_nla_get_ufid, __ovs_nla_copy_actions and the actions.c/conntrack.c consumers) dereference nlattr* parameters without in-helper NULL checks. The OVS datapath command handlers (ovs_dp_change, ovs_vport_cmd_set, ovs_flow_cmd_new/set) are reachable via the OVS genl family (GENL_UNS_ADMIN_PERM), but caller-side presence coverage for each helper parameter was not traced within this session's budget before the finalize directive; recorded as the primary remaining surface for this branch.

xfrm_user.c contains 8 helper functions dereferencing struct nlattr* parameters without own NULL checks (copy_to_user_* style parse helpers); xfrm netlink requires CAP_NET_ADMIN (xfrm_user_rcv_msg), satisfiable in a userns for some handlers; caller-side slot coverage not traced before finalize.

sch_netem.c has 7 nlattr-parameter helper candidates (netem qdisc option parsers consuming nested TCA_* attributes); net/sched kind init/change callbacks belong to the kind-callback-tb-gaps branch (i019); helper-parameter NULL-coverage not traced here.

seg6_local.c parse_nla_* callbacks (7 candidates) consume per-attribute nlattr* from the seg6local attribute table; the s01 twin audit (fact f014/i014) spot-checked these as caller-gated but the s03 instances were not re-verified line-by-line in this session.
devlink.c has 5 nlattr-parameter deref candidates in its command helpers; devlink genl ops are GENL_UNS_ADMIN_PERM (userns reachable); caller coverage not traced before finalize.

nl80211.c contains 8 helper-parameter candidates; nl80211 requires CFG80211 admin capability per op; the per-helper caller audit was not completed here (prior s03 artifacts also listed nl80211 as spot-check-only).

vxlan_fdb_parse (line ~1192) and other vxlan helpers consume tb[] slots as parameters without own NULL checks; the prior s03 rtnl audit (fact f008/i013) classified the vxlan_changelink->vxlan_nl2conf path unresolved; per-parameter coverage remains unverified (also listed for i019).

limitations: The helper-parameter surface was enumerated by a static scan over all .c files for functions taking 'struct nlattr *' (or a local holding a slot) that dereference the parameter (nla_get_*/nla_data/nla_len/nla_parse_nested*/nla_validate_nested*/nla_for_each_nested) without an in-function NULL check; 253 candidate functions in 99 files were found, of which only the i40e/ice br_spec flows (reported), lib/nlattr.c, nf_tables_api.c, and rtnetlink.c core (safe) were fully traced; the remaining clusters (openvswitch flow_netlink.c/actions.c/conntrack.c 43 sites, xfrm_user.c 8, sch_netem.c 7, seg6_local.c 7, cls_flower.c 5, devlink.c 5, macsec.c 5, plus ~170 more across 90 files) are unresolved and listed as the bounded remainder for this branch.

The two reported findings rest on the same static mechanism verified for the s02 twins (fact f003/i009): nlmsg_find_attr returning NULL for an absent optional attribute, nla_for_each_nested expanding to nla_data(nla)/nla_len(nla), and the rtnl_bridge_setlink BRIDGE_FLAGS_SELF raw-nlh forward at net/core/rtnetlink.c:4920; no runtime reproducer or compilation was run (read-only snapshot, no top-level Makefile/Kconfig), and triggering additionally requires an i40e or ice NIC present with the device up (a PF VSI in the vulnerable state), so impact on such hardware is a static hypothesis.

Permission reachability of RTM_SETLINK/PF_BRIDGE requires CAP_NET_ADMIN in the governing user namespace (satisfiable by an unprivileged user via unshare -Urn); the exact permission check on the rtnl_bridge_setlink doit dispatch was not re-verified line-by-line on this snapshot.

Search was truncated by the finalize directive: prior-session data (checkpoint + facts f002/f011/f008) was used to delimit the already-reported mac802154_hwsim.c handlers (not re-reported) and the already-audited safe sites (nl802154.c, macsec.c parse_sa_config, ip_vs_ctl.c, netlabel_cipso_v4.c, act_api.c find_dump_kind, mac80211_hwsim.c guards, l2tp_netlink.c, ncsi-netlink.c), so those files' helper-parameter surfaces were not re-scanned in this session.
Kernel-side dump/notify builders that only construct attributes were excluded from scope per the intent description; no negative proof is claimed for them.
